These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0013] Credits above 1000.00 need second approver: Finance policy FIN-2026-09 requires support-initiated refunds and credits above 1000.00 to have a second approver; enforce this in ledgerly/adjustments.py by raising BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is None.
  (learned from task S04 on ledgerly 2.0.0; source FIN-2026-09; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0011] Validate amounts with BillingError non_positive_amount: Validate monetary inputs by converting with to_money() then raising BillingError("non_positive_amount", str(amount)) when amount <= ZERO, matching ledgerly.payments.authorize.
  (learned from task S01 on ledgerly 2.0.0; relied on 2x, 2 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Record state changes via audit.record: Every payment/invoice state transition must emit an `audit.record("<entity>_<verb>", ...)` event with the entity id and amount, mirroring `payment_authorized`.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from money module: Normalize line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 3 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Guard draft status before mutating invoices: Before mutating an invoice, check `invoice.status != "draft"` and raise `BillingError("invalid_state", ...)` including the invoice id and status, matching `issue_invoice` in `ledgerly/invoice.py`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

- [at-0007] Money operations accept idempotency_key and check it first: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept a keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Check `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an existing entry with that key before any state validation and return the original record without reapplying; include `idempotency_key` in the `audit.record(...)` call.

texts.at-0001: Round money only via round_money Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Use to_money and ZERO from money module Normalize line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a stable snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and put the offending value in the detail via `repr`.
texts.at-0004: Guard draft status before mutating invoices Before mutating an invoice, check `invoice.status != "draft"` and raise `BillingError("invalid_state", ...)` including the invoice id and status, matching `issue_invoice` in `ledgerly/invoice.py`.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic; follow `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period` as the model.
texts.at-0006: Compute periods via timedelta floor division Billing periods are computed as `length = timedelta(days=sub.period_days)` and `n = (at - start) // length` from `ensure_utc(sub.started_at)`, as in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period`; reuse this pattern for renewal math.
